findings.anchor: query = f"SELECT id, status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = '{owner_id}'"
findings.body: owner_id is interpolated into the SQL string with an f-string and then passed to cursor.execute. Any quote or SQL fragment in that value changes the statement the database runs, including reading or modifying rows outside the intended customer. Bind owner_id as a query parameter (placeholder style must match this cursor's driver) and do not build the statement with string formatting.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller passes owner_id such as ' OR '1'='1 or a UNION payload; the query returns every order row or data from other tables through the same cursor.
findings.title: Parameterize owner_id to stop SQL injection

findings.anchor: def register_shipment_events(event_type: str, events: list[str] = []) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
findings.body: events defaults to a single list object created at function definition time, and the body appends event_type onto that list before returning it. Later calls that omit events therefore see every previous caller's event types. If an empty default is required, use None and assign a new list inside the function; do not mutate the default.
findings.failure_scenario: Request A records a shipment event type, then request B calls register_shipment_events without its own list and receives A's event types in the returned mapping.

findings.body: The function sorts every record to read a single id, which is O(n log n) and allocates another list. The docstring promises constant time under chronological arrival; if that assumption cannot be trusted, one `max` pass still finds the same record without sorting.
findings.failure_scenario: A long queue history makes every newest-id lookup sort the full record list, adding latency that grows faster than the input on a path documented as constant time.

findings.body: The zone and weight loops do not use carrier, so the same viable count is recomputed from scratch for every carrier. The nested scans are O(carriers × zones × weights) where a single pass over zones and weights would do.
findings.failure_scenario: Large zone, weight, and carrier lists make cross_check_tariff_routes repeat the same nested scan once per carrier, multiplying CPU time with no change in the result.
findings.title: Hoist the carrier-independent count

findings.body: The inner loops never read carrier, so every carrier is assigned the same count and the three-deep loop just repeats one product. Viable pairs are positive weights times non-empty zones; compute that once and map it onto the carriers.
findings.title: Hoist the carrier-independent route count

findings.body: seen and labels are appended on the same path and never diverge, so they always hold the same strings. The second list is a name to keep in sync and makes the loop look like it tracks two different sets. Test membership on labels and append once.

findings.anchor: query = f"SELECT id, status, total FROM orders WHERE customer_id = '{owner_id}'"
findings.body: owner_id is concatenated into the SQL string with an f-string and handed to cursor.execute. Any quote or SQL fragment in that value becomes part of the statement, so the WHERE clause can be rewritten or extended. Pass owner_id as a bound parameter (driver placeholder such as %s or ?) on cursor.execute, and do not build the predicate by string formatting.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller supplies owner_id as ' OR '1'='1 (or a UNION payload). The query no longer filters to one customer and returns other customers' order ids, statuses, and totals; stacked statements may run if the driver allows them.
findings.title: SQL injection: bind owner_id instead of interpolating it

findings.anchor: def register_shipment_events(event_type: str, events: list[str] = []) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
findings.body: events defaults to one list created at function definition. Calls that omit the argument append to that same object and then return a copy of its full contents, so later callers receive event types recorded by earlier callers. Use events: list[str] | None = None and assign events = [] inside the function when it is None before appending.

findings.body: load_order_rows builds the orders query with an f-string, so owner_id is concatenated into the SQL text before cursor.execute. findings.body: The default events=[] is created once and reused for every call that omits the argument. events.append(event_type) then writes the type name into that shared list, so later calls see earlier types and the returned mapping mixes unrelated events under the current key. findings.failure_scenario: register_shipment_events('shipped') followed by register_shipment_events('delivered') returns {'delivered': ['shipped', 'delivered']} instead of only the delivered events.
findings.title: Stop sharing a mutable default events list
